<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/field.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-list.mdx`  _(via formView (literal, a string literal in validateInternalFormViews))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via FormViewSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/index.mdx`  _(via FormViewSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`  _(via FormViewSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/ui/create-vs-edit-form.mdx`  _(via showOnCreate (literal, a string literal in sections))_
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx`  _(via showOnCreate (literal, a string literal in sections))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via FormViewSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via formView (literal, a string literal in validateInternalFormViews))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/field.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87c7bbaf45799f0f2e5996a00c49a7d4a731c2b7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f429ee1265cbdd2934bfdfddd60bf2c42232a475` — the merge of head `deb499072fff61c284a6794a3a2e9a9b65687eda` into base `87c7bbaf45799f0f2e5996a00c49a7d4a731c2b7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f429ee1265cbdd2934bfdfddd60bf2c42232a475 && git checkout f429ee1265cbdd2934bfdfddd60bf2c42232a475
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 87c7bbaf45799f0f2e5996a00c49a7d4a731c2b7 deb499072fff61c284a6794a3a2e9a9b65687eda && git checkout -B drift-repro 87c7bbaf45799f0f2e5996a00c49a7d4a731c2b7 && git merge --no-ff deb499072fff61c284a6794a3a2e9a9b65687eda

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87c7bbaf45799f0f2e5996a00c49a7d4a731c2b7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 87c7bbaf45799f0f2e5996a00c49a7d4a731c2b7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

SKIPPED on a pull request: the three dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts. The green "Dogfood Regression Gate" row is the aggregate over skipped shards, not a dogfood run.

### ① Derived judgments

- Parse accept-set: unchanged. No hunk touches `view.zod.ts` or `field.zod.ts`; every form-view key still parses on every form. `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is the right kind (a kept key changes meaning). Right.
- Consumer: the object's default form (`form`, `formViews.default`, an `isDefault` form item) and its `OBJECT.create` form stop steering the create dialog, the edit dialog, `RecordFormPage` and `useActionModal`; `selectRecordFormView` and `resolveFormViewLayout` are deleted and nothing else called them. This is card items 1, 4 and 10 and the maintainer's 「现有的可以不加载」 and 「平台不加载了，再慢慢迁移」. Right as a direction.
- Sub-tables: `attachInlineSubforms` now writes `groupSubforms` and no longer merges an authored `form.subforms`. So an explicit `subforms` on the default form is dropped on create, edit and the flow screen, where the card's item 2 named only the flow screen. Item 1 (「一律按对象的字段分组排」) covers it, and the new upgrade entry names `fieldGroups[].relatedList`. No example in this repo authors `subforms` (grep at head: zero). Right. Not verified: whether `relatedList` can express every `subforms` option (`amountField`, `totalField`, `minRows`, `maxRows`).
- Named and public forms: at the merge-base the only readers of an object's `form` / `formViews` in `ui/packages/app-shell/src` were the default and `OBJECT.create` lookups this PR deletes. `FormPage` loads a named or public form by its own name and is not in the diff. No path that honoured a named form before ignores it now. Right.
- `showOnCreate`: one helper (`recordFormFieldNames` over `isFieldAskedOnFlow`) feeds the dialog, the full page and the action modal; the lookup field's inline create goes through `useActionModal`. A reader exists in shipped code, so the ledger flip to `live` is true for those three. It is not true for the flow screen: S1.
- `field.form.ts` row, its eleven locale entries and the deleted omit row: the switch is offered in the change that lands its readers. Right.
- Lint: `form-view-internal-not-loaded` is advisory, CLI-only, on every check command; it fires on a container's `form`, `formViews.default`, `formViews.create`, and a form item that is `isDefault` or named `OBJECT.create`; `sharing.enabled === true` and every other name are exempt. That is the card's one test. Right, with N2.
- Semantic entry: 18 is the current protocol major (spec 18.6.0; 568 sibling entries under 18). File name, shape and the four prose fields match its siblings, and it names the views and the keys the changeset names. Right in itself; it now contradicts a sibling entry of the same major: M2.
- Public surface: `@objectstack/lint` gains `validateInternalFormViews`, `FORM_VIEW_INTERNAL_NOT_LOADED` and `InternalFormViewFinding`; `@object-ui/i18n` gains two studio keys and loses eight. See N1.
- Upgrade, what a user sees: sections become field groups; fields a form left out appear; a `required`, `readonly` or `visibleWhen` written on a form field entry stops applying; form `defaults`, `buttons`, tabs, wizard steps and `modalSize` stop applying. No required object field is hidden (the parse refuses `showOnCreate: false` beside `required: true`). The card lists these three effects as known to the maintainer. No platform object declares an internal form (grep at head: zero).

### ② Semver level

Changeset: spec minor, lint minor, app-shell minor, platform-objects patch, i18n patch, with both declaration lines and one ADR-0087 marker (`registered internal-record-forms-not-loaded`), and the FROM to TO prescription in its last paragraphs. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head. The `(narrowing)` arm is the breaking carrier `check-adr-0087-registration` reads; its lane had not all concluded when this was written.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — as declared. The arm is right: honoured behaviour is withdrawn. The value is arguable, see N1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation, full dogfood battery not run: answered, and escalated to the seat. `os-dev.md` owes the whole battery once at the final head on a `(narrowing)` arm. It was run by path only (2 files), and the pull-request run skips the shards. So no dogfood verdict exists for this head from any source; the merge queue is the first place it runs. This record certifies nothing about it.
- Dev deviation, semantic entry outside the claimed file surface: accepted. The ADR-0087 gate requires a disposition and this is the right one.
- Dev deviation, `view.json` notes for `type` and `modalSize`, four docs transcripts, the catalog pin: accepted; each follows from the diff.
- Dev deviation, model-free commit trailers: not a contract matter; left to the seat.
- Open question, `form.modalSize` ledger verdict: answered A. It is carried by #36544. The schema text that goes with it is part of M2.
- Out-of-scope note, HotCRM create defaults NOT MEASURED: stands as not measured; the card excludes HotCRM.
- Security: no authorization boundary moves. A form view was never a write gate; the API accepted a field the form left out. What changes is exposure in the Console: a field the default form omitted, or marked `readonly` on its form entry, is now drawn and editable in New and Edit for a user who could already write it. Field-level permissions are not touched by the diff.
- SQL push-down: no query, id materialisation or in-app join is added. Nothing to report.
- Seat ruling 4 (`requiredWhen` with `showOnCreate: false` is accepted): a create can then be refused for a field the dialog does not draw. Ruled; noted, not graded.
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no other login to name. The PR is a draft.

### ④ Design judgment

The central question. The published spec at this head still declares the capability this PR withdraws, because `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` is not in the diff. The maintainer ruled the retirement, so withdrawing it is legitimate and is not a consumer-side narrowing of something the maintainer wants kept. But a retirement has to be made at the spec as well, and here the spec still declares it and in one place still prescribes it. The lint rule, the new upgrade entry, the changeset and the two ledger notes are the right half of the kit. The other half is missing.

M1 (must-fix) — the new rule fires on `examples/app-showcase` and its pin is not updated. `examples/app-showcase/test/author-time-advisories.test.ts` runs `validate --json` and fails on any finding not on `ALLOWED_ADVISORIES` ("fix the metadata it names, or add it here with its reason, in the same change"). At this head the showcase still declares internal forms with no public sharing: `form` in `task.view.ts`, `business-unit.view.ts`, `project.view.ts`, and `form` plus `formViews.create` in `contact.view.ts`. The rule is registered exactly as `validateFieldConsumers` is, whose `field-no-consumers` finding is on that list, so its warnings reach the same report. No `examples/**` path is in the diff and the list holds no `form-view-internal-not-loaded` entry. This is read, not run: Test Core was pending. If it concludes green the finding is wrong and closes. The fix has to choose: migrate the showcase forms to field groups, or allow-list each with a reason. The source comments there ("The default form — what the create and edit surfaces render") and `app-crm`'s `lead.view.ts` say the same false thing.

M2 (must-fix) — the published spec still prescribes the retired convention. In `view.zod.ts` at this head: (a) the `addRecord.formView` tombstone, a parse error an author receives, says "to give the Add button its own form declare it as `formViews.create` on the object's view container (without one, the default form is used)"; (b) the `AddRecordConfig` JSDoc says "The create form is chosen by convention: `formViews.create` when declared, else `form` / `formViews.default`"; (c) the `type: 'modal'` prescription says the New and Edit dialogs are "sized by the form's `modalSize`"; (d) the `modalSize` description, published in the JSON schema and the reference pages, names "the console's New / Edit dialog". And `semantic/18.add-record-mode-form-view-retired.ts` tells an upgrader to declare `formViews.create`, with an acceptance criterion that requires it, in the same protocol-18 guide where this PR's entry says that form is not loaded. After this PR an author who follows the spec's own error message writes a form that does nothing and draws the new warning. That is a capability declared and not delivered, created by this diff. Correct (a), (b), (c) and the sibling entry here; (d) may ride #36544 if the PR says so.

S1 (should-fix) — `showOnCreate` is declared for every create surface and one does not read it. The key's description says "`false`: no create surface shows it", and the ledger row now says `live` because "every create surface of the Console leaves a `showOnCreate: false` field out". `ScreenView` draws an object form in `mode: 'create'` with no `fields` list, so a flow screen shows the field. The PR body says so and leaves it. Either hand `ScreenView`'s create the same `recordFormFieldNames` list, or narrow the description and the ledger note to the surfaces that read it.

S2 (should-fix) — `Skills-docs: follow-up #36455` names a card that covers `skills/**` only. `content/docs/ui/create-vs-edit-form.mdx` is a whole page teaching `formViews.create`, and `content/docs/ui/views.mdx` (Form View) says "`form` is the object's default form — the create and edit surfaces render it" and that `formViews.create` "is the form every create entry opens". No card carries them. File one, or widen #36455, and name it on the PR body line.

N1 (nit) — `Clause-②: no` beside new `@objectstack/lint` exports and new published locale keys. By the criterion (does it widen the public surface) the value reads `yes (narrowing)`. `.changeset/34776-publish-checks-build-probes.md` on `main` added lint exports under `no (narrowing)`, so this is an accepted deviation unless the seat wants the line changed on the prose faces.

N2 (nit) — the rule and the Interfaces rail call a default or `OBJECT.create` form internal even when a `form`-type action opens it by that name, where `FormPage` still loads it. The message "no longer loaded" overstates for that case and the Studio stops listing a form that is reachable. Advisory only. Follow-up card.

N3 (nit) — comments in `FormPage.tsx` and three plugin-form tests still name the deleted `resolveFormViewLayout`. The PR body lists them. Follow-up.
